_comment: THE REVIEWED DESTINATION POLICY for the PostgreSQL copy fence.
Read by pg-copy-ops.ts via --destination-policy. Every reviewed label must
appear exactly once, in the reviewed order, and each entry DECLARES two
separate facts that the census then COMPARES against what it measured:
installation - whether the agent is installed, and how launchd holds it
expected     - which database it writes to, if any
Neither is inferred. A census that measured something the policy did not
declare refuses, in both directions: an agent found loaded when the policy
says unloaded, and an agent found unloaded when the policy says loaded.
CURRENT STATE, after the S4F-D5-K5 runtime cutover: the four production
plists are installed under ~/Library/LaunchAgents while their labels are
booted out, so each is 'installed-unloaded'. They name the pipeline
credential container, which points at the copy source, so each is
'writes-copy-source'. The structured worker is not installed on this
machine at all - no label and no plist - so it is 'expected-absent' in both
columns, and every one of its evidence fields is null by contract.
'installed-unloaded' is NOT 'expected-absent'. The first binds a complete
identity - plist path, plist digest, plist device:inode, served checkout,
credential container identity and sanitized endpoint - because all of those
exist and were measured. The second binds nothing, because there is nothing
to measure. Collapsing the first onto the second is the defect S4F-D5-K5.2
closed: it dropped four installed plists out of the operational binding, so
one could be replaced between two censuses without moving the confirmation
token.
